rationale: Evidence from iteration 1 (60 trials, none finished) shows the widened-sensor change made things worse. Score fell from 84.6 to 53.5. Oval progress dropped from 0.35 to 0.19 and line-loss events rose from 1.15 to 2.4. Only the s-bend improved on line losses (1.0 to 0.35). max_error stayed at 0.061 to 0.063 on every track, which is the off-track limit. Widening the sensors therefore did not stop the robot leaving the track, so the Evaluator's hypothesis that sensor blindness was the root cause is not supported. The off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4). Even at body_width 0.18 this is 0.0575, so it is effectively fixed at 0.06 m. The fix has to come from keeping lateral error below 0.06 m on bends. Changes: (1) Geometry reverts to the iteration 0 layout (x = -0.04 to +0.04, 0.02 spacing, 12 mm sensors), the best-scoring evidence. (2) kp goes from 5.0 to 3.0. The iteration 1 oval showed more line losses with the high gain, and the iteration 0 gain of 2.5 was the best result so far. (3) kd stays at 0.4 (up from 0.2) to damp the approach into bends, since rms error is low and the spikes are at the bends. (4) base_speed drops from 1.2 to 1.0. The robot leaves the line on sharp bends at speed, and lower speed should reduce overshoot and line loss. Progress is the scored quantity while nothing finishes, so covering more of the course matters more than raw speed for now. Expected result: line_loss_events at or below 1.0 per run, max_error below 0.06 on at least the s-bend, and oval progress above 0.35. Hypotheses to check next: (a) if max_error still hits 0.06 at base_speed 1.0, the bend error is controller lag and ki or a higher kd is needed; (b) if progress falls with no loss reduction, speed was not the cause and kp 2.5 should be restored; (c) if the robot is stable with spare time, raise base_speed in steps of 0.2 to test whether speed can be recovered without going off track.
